title: The Aklan People
description: The Province of Aklan is home to the indigenous Ati people and the Aklanon-speaking communities who have long inhabited the region, known for their distinct culture, language, and traditions.

title: Spanish Colonization
description: Spanish missionaries establish missions in the area of present-day Aklan, beginning the Christianization and reorganization of communities into pueblos.

title: Ati-Atihan Origins
description: The Ati-Atihan Festival in Kalibo begins as a celebration of the Ati people and the arrival of Malay datus from Borneo, becoming one of the Philippines' oldest and most celebrated festivals.

title: Province of Aklan Established
description: Aklan was officially established as a separate province from Capiz by virtue of Republic Act 2711 (Revised Administrative Code), with Kalibo as its capital.

title: Republic Act 1414
description: Republic Act 1414 formally reconstituted Aklan as a full province, organizing its 17 municipalities under unified provincial governance.

title: Boracay Discovery
description: Boracay Island (in Malay, Aklan) gains international recognition as one of the world's finest beach destinations, transforming Aklan into a global tourism hub.

title: Boracay Rehabilitation
description: The national government undertakes a landmark 6-month closure and rehabilitation of Boracay Island to restore its environmental quality, followed by a structured reopening under strict regulations.

title: Progressive and Sustainable Aklan
description: The Province of Aklan continues to develop under the vision of becoming 'Progressive and Sustainable Aklan,' balancing tourism development, agricultural growth, environmental protection, and improved public services for all 17 municipalities.
